criteria.criterion: ProducerInputs and VerifierInputs in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs gain an optional pin (athena_data PinnedRepo: url, ref, sha); producer_brief and verifier_brief render a 'Pinned source' section with all three values only when it is set, and omit it otherwise.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. Both structs gain `pub pin: Option<PinnedRepo>`. A new `pin_section` writes '## Pinned source' with url, git_ref and sha only when the pin is `Some`. `producer_brief` and `verifier_brief` both call it, after `reading_sections`.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/run.rs passes the pin resolved by pin_repo into the producer brief (and into the verifier inputs), so the brief carries the real resolved SHA, never a placeholder.
criteria.evidence: I read run.rs. Line 213 builds the producer brief from `pinned` (the value `pin_repo` returns at line 191); it is the same value that goes into the job record's `pin` at line 254. Line 756 builds the verifier inputs from `ctx.job.job.pin`, and `ctx.job.job` is set to that same job record at line 275. run_pin_tests.rs now reads the committed brief-producer.md and asserts it contains the URL and `sha: {FAKE_SHA}`.

criteria.criterion: The VERIFIER_VISIBILITY text no longer forbids citing the pinned SHA: it still bars hashes made during verification, but states that the pinned instance's url, ref and SHA from the brief must be cited as given.
criteria.evidence: The text now reads: 'never pin or cite a commit hash made during verification … The one exception is the pinned instance: when the brief has a "Pinned source" section, cite its url, ref and SHA as given.' A search under crates/ found no other copy of the hash rule, so neither prompts/producer.md nor prompts/verifier.md needed changes.

criteria.criterion: New unit tests in briefs.rs show a brief with a pin contains the url, ref and full SHA and the exemption wording, and a brief without a pin has no pin section. Run: cargo test -p athena-context.
criteria.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-context`: 20 passed. The new tests are producer_briefs_carry_the_pin_with_the_exemption_when_set, producer_briefs_without_a_pin_have_no_pin_section and verifier_briefs_carry_the_pin_only_when_set. Together they assert the url, `ref: main`, the full 40-character SHA, the exemption wording, and that the section is absent when the pin is None.

criteria.criterion: Existing tests (including the one asserting the hash rule wording) are updated and pass, and the core's study pin tests still pass. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check.
criteria.evidence: producer_briefs_say_what_the_verifier_can_see now asserts the new wording, and it passes. `cargo test --locked` passed in every crate, including run_pin_tests::a_study_pins_once_records_the_commit_and_mounts_it_read_only_for_both_agents. Clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` both exited cleanly.

findings.summary: No core-level test checks that the verifier brief carries the pin; only the producer brief is checked end to end.
findings.evidence: run_pin_tests.rs adds checks on brief-producer.md only. The verifier wiring at run.rs:756 is covered only by the unit test in briefs.rs, which builds VerifierInputs directly.

findings.summary: The 'no pin' test asserts that the brief does not contain 'sha:'. That could break if unrelated brief text ever includes the string 'sha:'.

summary: The change passes. When a job pins a repository, its producer and verifier briefs now include a "Pinned source" section with the url, ref and full SHA. These values come from the pin that `pin_repo` resolved and that is stored in the job record, so the brief can no longer carry a placeholder. The hash rule now forbids only commit hashes made during verification, and it tells the producer to cite the pinned url, ref and SHA as given. Briefs without a pin are unchanged. New unit tests cover the section being present and absent and the new rule wording, and the core study-pin test now checks that the committed producer brief contains the real SHA. I ran `cargo test -p athena-context`, `cargo test --locked`, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; all passed. Two small findings: no core-level test checks that the verifier brief carries the pin (only the producer brief is checked end to end), and the "no pin" test checks for the absence of the general string 'sha:'.
